guides.name: Philippines
guides.title: Meetings in Manila. Then the islands.
guides.sub: We host business visitors and holiday groups from China and around the world, from the arrivals hall to the departure gate — in Mandarin, English or Filipino. This is what we tell every client before they book a flight.

entry.d: Since 16 January 2026, 14 days without a visa for tourism or business — but only when you land at Manila (NAIA) or Cebu (Mactan). The stay cannot be extended or changed to another visa. Bring a passport valid six months beyond your stay, your confirmed hotel booking and a return or onward ticket. Staying longer, or flying into Clark, Davao or another airport? Apply for a temporary visitor visa before you travel; we prepare the invitation letter and itinerary.

14 days visa-free for tourism, or 30 days if you hold a valid US, Japanese, Australian, Canadian, Schengen, Singapore or UK visa or residence permit. Coming for business meetings? Tell us — the right visa depends on what you will be doing.
A visa is needed before you travel, from a Philippine embassy or consulate. We send the invitation letter, hotel confirmation and itinerary the application asks for.
Many nationalities get 30 days visa-free on arrival; some need a visa first. Send us your passport country and we confirm what applies before you book.
Register free at etravel.gov.ph within 72 hours before you land. You get a QR code that airline check-in and immigration will ask for. Any site that charges for it is not the government's.

guides.entryNote: Immigration officers do ask about your trip. Keep your hotel booking, return ticket and our itinerary letter on your phone or on paper. Entry rules change often — we confirm yours when you book.

fly.d: Direct flights from Beijing, Shanghai, Guangzhou, Shenzhen and Xiamen — about 2½ hours from South China, 4 to 4½ from Beijing.
Direct from Shanghai, Guangzhou, Shenzhen and Quanzhou. Cebu is the better gateway for Bohol and the central islands.
Connections through Hong Kong, Singapore and Bangkok, and direct flights to Manila from Dubai and Abu Dhabi.
Clark International, two hours north of Manila, is quicker to get through — but the visa-free entry for Chinese passports does not apply there.

guides.whereTitle: Manila is six cities in one.

where.d: The established business district: banks, law firms, embassies and the long-standing hotels.
Bonifacio Global City: newer towers, regional headquarters and the most walkable streets in Manila. Where most of our clients stay.
Corporate and retail headquarters, and SM Megamall, one of the country's largest malls.
Founded in 1594 and often called the world's oldest Chinatown. Filipino-Chinese trading families, wholesalers and chambers — and the markets where you see what goods really sell for.
The convention centres — SMX and the World Trade Center — and the large resort hotels near the airport.
Clark and Subic freeports to the north for logistics and light manufacturing; Cebu for furniture, export zones and the Visayas; Davao for agriculture and Mindanao.

guides.moveTitle: How we move you around Manila.
move: Plan two meetings a day, three at most. A 10 km drive across Metro Manila can take over an hour at peak time.
A car and driver stay with you all day. The driver waits outside every meeting; nobody stands in a taxi queue.
Stay near your meetings — BGC or Makati for most weeks, closer to Binondo if your week is with the Filipino-Chinese trade.
Domestic flights and boat transfers get buffer time. On the islands the weather decides, not the timetable.
From June to November typhoons can close airports for a day. We build a spare day into trips in those months.
Grab works well if you want to move on your own; we set it up on your phone when you land.
guides.chinaTitle: The details that make the trip easy.

china.d: Mandarin-speaking guides and interpreters every day of the trip; Cantonese and Hokkien on request — Hokkien is the home language of many Filipino-Chinese families.
The Philippines runs on UTC+8, like Beijing. Your office in China is awake when you are working.
WeChat works normally. Filipino business runs on Viber and Messenger, so we set up the groups with your local contacts.
Cards work in hotels and malls. Alipay and WeChat Pay are taken at some malls, hotels and duty-free shops — not everywhere. We arrange pesos and a local SIM or eSIM when you land.
Chinese restaurants we know in Binondo, Makati and BGC for the business dinners; Filipino food when you want it.
Introductions to Filipino-Chinese trading families and chambers — often the fastest way into distribution.

guides.islandsTitle: Add three days. It is the part they talk about.

islands.time: About an hour's flight from Manila
islands.d: Limestone lagoons, island hopping and some of Asia's best beaches. Our first choice for incentive groups.

islands.time: About an hour's flight, then a short boat
islands.d: White Beach, sunsets and easy resorts. Good for families and first visits.

islands.time: An hour from Manila, or two by ferry from Cebu
islands.d: The Chocolate Hills, tarsiers, river cruises and Panglao's beaches.
Island hopping from Mactan, waterfalls and diving on the south coast; easy to pair with Bohol.
Surf, palm forests and a slower pace.

islands.time: Day trips by road or ferry
islands.d: Tagaytay and Taal Volcano, the walled city of Intramuros, and Corregidor island.
